resources.string: Choose the Files the Deck Uses
An app for slides written in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. Open a .kt file (or a folder of them) that declares `val deck = presentation { … }`. It reloads every time you save.
Compiling %1$s… (the first build may take a while)
A deck is a program. Opening it runs its code with your permissions, so it can read your files and use the network. Open only decks you trust. You will not be asked again for this folder.
A deck is a program. Opening it runs its code with your permissions, so it can read your files and use the network. Open only decks you trust. You will not be asked again for this file.

A theme is a program, like a deck. Loading it runs its code with your permissions, so it can read your files and use the network. Load only themes you trust. You will not be asked again for this file.
The jars in libs/ run as programs too. Unlike .kt files, a jar can’t be checked by opening it in an editor.

In safe mode the slides’ code runs in a sandbox: it can draw the slides but cannot read your files (only the system, the app, installed fonts and a copy of the deck), reach the network, or start other apps. Slides with heavy motion may stutter.
Opening “%1$s” in safe mode… (the first build may take a while)
Could not open in safe mode
The process drawing the slides in safe mode stopped. Close the deck and open it again.
Can’t open in safe mode: “%1$s” has another hard link.
Can’t open in safe mode: the deck’s folder is too large (up to %1$s files and folders, %2$d GB).
Can’t open in safe mode: “%1$s” is not in the deck’s folder.
Choose Files and Open in Safe Mode…
In safe mode, a deck of one file reads that file alone. If it uses images or other files, choose them too, from the deck’s folder.
